title: Metabolic clinics & dietitian network
source_note: Compiled from NPKUA/BioMarin/KUVAN clinic finders, hospital metabolic-program pages, GMDI, regional genetics collaboratives (SERN/NECMP), and peer-reviewed access studies (Nature Genetics in Medicine, Orphanet JRD, MDPI Nutrients). Care-delivery/market view only — no clinical protocols. Clinic-level adult_care and telehealth flags are 'unknown' where the program page did not state a policy; PKU care is concentrated at ~90-120 US metabolic centers and dedicated adult PKU clinics are rare.

records.name: PKU care is concentrated at ~90–120 US metabolic centers
records.notes: Specialty PKU care clusters at children's hospitals and academic medical centers reachable only via clinic-finder tools (NPKUA, BioMarin, KUVAN). The concentration creates real travel/access burden for rural patients and is the core market gap.

sources.title: Find a Local PKU Clinic — BioMarin
Find a Specialized PKU Clinic — KUVAN

records.name: Adult PKU access gap: >70% of US adults not in specialty care
records.notes: Patient, social, and economic factors keep more than 70% of US adults with PKU from accessing treatment; many are 'lost to follow-up.' Dedicated adult PKU clinics are scarce, so adults are often held over in pediatric centers — the single largest unmet-need signal in PKU care delivery.

sources.title: Newborn screening 50 years later: access issues faced by adults with PKU (Genetics in Medicine)
Adult patient perspectives on PKU care: need for dedicated adult management (PubMed)

records.name: Metabolic dietitian shortage: ~133 patients per RD FTE and rising
records.notes: GMDI professional-status surveys show median caseload rising to 133 patients per dietitian FTE (2020), up from 124 (2017) and 120 (2013). Burnout and overwhelming ratios are top challenges — the dietitian layer, not physicians, is the binding constraint on PKU care capacity.

sources.title: Compensation for metabolic dietitians in the US: 2023 GMDI survey (PMC)
Examining Roles, Challenges, and Opportunities Within the Metabolic Genetics Workforce (AJMG-A)

records.name: GMDI — Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (professional body)
records.notes: Founded 2005; the profession's standards body for metabolic nutrition. Runs a Job Connection board (a live labor-shortage signal), a mentorship program, and co-authors the national nutrition-management guidelines with SERN.

records.name: SERN / SERC — Southeast Regional Genetics Network nutrition guidelines
records.notes: HRSA-funded regional collaborative that, with GMDI, produced evidence- and consensus-based nutrition-management guidelines for PKU and other IMDs — the shared clinical infrastructure many clinics rely on. Serves AL, GA, FL, LA, MS, NC, SC, TN.

sources.title: Nutrition Management Guidelines — Southeast Regional Genetics Network

records.name: New England Consortium of Metabolic Programs (NECMP)
records.location: New England (CT, ME, MA, NH, RI, VT)
records.notes: Regional consortium coordinating metabolic clinics across six New England states — a model for pooling scarce specialty capacity across small states.

sources.title: New England Consortium of Metabolic Programs

records.name: HRSA Regional Genetics Networks (RGN) — national coordinating layer
records.notes: The NCC/RC system organizes US genetic/metabolic care into regional networks (e.g., SERN, plus Mountain States, Western States, Heartland, Mid-Atlantic, New England, New York-Mid-Atlantic). Federal telehealth and access-equity mandates run through this layer — the policy channel for closing rural gaps.

sources.title: The NCC/RC System at 10 Years: A Look Back
SERN — National Coordinating Center for the Regional Genetics Networks

records.name: Telehealth metabolic nutrition — emerging access category
records.notes: Video/hybrid dietitian counseling has high patient acceptance (~90% would recommend) and is the most credible near-term lever for the rural + adult + dietitian-shortage gaps. Still nascent for PKU specifically; a whitespace for branded remote metabolic-nutrition services.

sources.title: Telehealth for Nutritional Care: improving patient flow (PMC)

records.name: Patient-organization clinic finders are the de-facto market directory
records.notes: No single authoritative public registry of PKU clinics exists; patients navigate via advocacy/manufacturer finders (NPKUA, BioMarin, KUVAN) and state groups (Georgia PKU Connect, CCPKUAD, Maternal PKU Support). Fragmented discovery is itself an access barrier and a data-product opportunity.

records.name: Maternal PKU: preconception access gap compounds the adult gap
records.notes: Women with PKU who fell out of adult specialty care face high fetal risk; gaps in preconception metabolic care are documented. Maternal PKU is a high-acuity subsegment where the adult-care shortage has the steepest clinical and cost consequences.
